items.topic: Is this fix already implemented or still needed?
items.context: Reading the codebase, handler.go already contains effort normalization logic (ToUpper + TrimSpace) on both create and update paths, and handler_test.go has 6 test cases covering the scenarios. The proto schemas and types.go also include the Effort field. It's possible this fix was already completed as part of the recent backlog changes (the files show as modified in git status). If so, the item just needs verification and can be closed.

options.label: Already implemented — verify and close
options.rationale: The code and tests already exist. Run the tests, confirm they pass, and mark this item as completed.

options.label: Partially implemented — needs additional work
options.rationale: The basic logic exists but there are edge cases or integration issues that still need fixing. Describe what's missing in freeform.

options.label: Not yet implemented — code is staged but untested
options.rationale: The code exists in modified files but hasn't been verified to work correctly yet.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the current state in freeform.

items.notes: Recommended: The implementation appears complete based on code review. The handler normalizes effort on create (line 114-118) and update (line 418-423), validateEffort() rejects invalid values (line 128-139), and 6 test cases cover the matrix.

items.context: The batch handler (batch_handler.go) also creates backlog items. If effort normalization only happens in the single-item create handler, batch-created items might bypass normalization. Need to verify the batch path also normalizes.

options.label: Yes — add normalization to batch handler
options.rationale: Consistency requires all creation paths normalize effort. If batch handler delegates to the same create logic, this may already be covered.

options.label: Not needed — batch delegates to shared logic
options.rationale: If batch-create calls the same validation/normalization functions, no additional work needed.

options.label: Defer to separate item
options.rationale: Batch effort normalization is a separate concern — track it independently.

items.topic: Should the CLI normalize effort client-side?
items.context: Currently the plan marks CLI-side validation as out of scope (API is authoritative). However, providing early feedback in the CLI (before the API call) improves UX. The tradeoff is duplicating validation logic.

options.label: No — API-only normalization
options.rationale: Single source of truth for validation. CLI sends raw input, API normalizes. Simpler maintenance.

options.label: Yes — add CLI-side normalization
options.rationale: Better UX with immediate feedback. Low cost since it's just ToUpper on a known set.

options.label: Defer
options.rationale: Address in a future CLI improvement pass.

items.notes: Recommended: API-only keeps validation logic in one place. The CLI already displays API error messages clearly.

items.topic: How to handle the test-created backlog items?
items.context: The tests (TestCreate_WithEffort, TestCreate_EffortNormalizesCase, TestCreate_EffortOptional) use item names that match actual backlog items on disk: ideas/effort-test, fix/effort-case-test, ideas/no-effort. These appear as untracked/modified in git. The tests themselves use t.TempDir() and are properly isolated, so these on-disk items were likely created separately (perhaps by running the initialization skill on them). They should be cleaned up or acknowledged.

options.label: Clean up — delete the spurious backlog items
options.rationale: These items have empty descriptions and serve no purpose beyond testing the effort field. Remove them from the backlog.

options.label: Keep as test fixtures
options.rationale: They serve as examples of effort field usage and can be referenced.

options.label: Archive them
options.rationale: Move to archived status to keep history but remove from active backlog.

items.topic: Should proto schema include effort validation?
items.context: The proto backlog schema was modified to include the effort field. Proto supports enums which could enforce valid values at the schema level rather than relying solely on Go-side validation. However, string fields are more flexible and the Go validation is already comprehensive.

options.label: Keep as string in proto
options.rationale: Simpler, matches current implementation. Validation stays in Go. Adding values later doesn't require proto regeneration.

options.label: Use proto enum
options.rationale: Schema-level enforcement. All language bindings get valid values automatically. Requires proto regeneration when values change.

items.notes: Recommended: String is simpler and already validated server-side. Proto enum adds regeneration overhead for minimal benefit since the API is the only entry point.

items.text: The effort field implementation appears complete across all layers: types.go (BacklogItem.Effort + validateEffort()), handler.go (create/update normalization), store.go (proto mapping), and handler_test.go (6 test cases). The proto schemas also show as modified in git status with effort field additions.

Related backlog items 'ideas/effort-test' and 'ideas/no-effort' were also initialized with workshop rounds. They appear to be artifacts from testing the effort field feature rather than genuine ideas — both have empty descriptions and all-TBD plans.
